claims.text: RWY frames a “basic question” of seeking more efficient generators for \(I_w\); this passage does not state a polynomial-size bound. [doi:10.1090/s0002-9947-2010-05163-3, lines 89-106]

groundings.excerpt:
89: Therefore, a basic question is to request more efficient generating
90: sets for I_{w}. For type A_{n-1}, earlier work
91: [ GR02 ] reduced the |W|=n! upper bound on the number
92: of generators for I_{w} to a polynomial bound of n^{2} for the class
93: of Schubert varieties X_{w} defined by inclusions ; this class
94: includes all smooth X_{w}. Moreover, for a certain subclass of smooth
95: Schubert varieties X_{w} considered originally by Ding
96: [ D97 , D01 ] , they gave a smaller generating set for these I_{w}
97: having only n generators. This latter result was applied in
98: [ DMR07 ] to classify these varieties up to
99: isomorphism and homeomorphism (the generating set ( 1.2 )
100: having proved too unwieldy). One motivation for this work arises from
101: the desire to extend this classification to general Schubert varieties of
102: type A. Experience suggests that presentations for I_{w} that are
103: as simple as possible are best for this purpose.
104: The question of finding
105: simple presentations of I_{w} for other root systems appears to

claims.text: RWY says it conjectures that its smaller type-\(A\) generating set for \(J_v\) is minimal and explains the conditional exponential lower-bound consequence. [doi:10.1090/s0002-9947-2010-05163-3, lines 202-211]

groundings.excerpt:
202: Actually, we conjecture that this smaller generating set for J_{v} in
203: type A is minimal (although the generating set ( 1.6 )
204: for I_{w} obtained by concatenation is not always minimal; see
205: Example 4.12 .) The significance of this
206: minimality conjecture, as explained in Section 4.5 , is that
207: it implies an exponential lower bound of at least
208: \binom{n/2}{n/4}\sim\frac{{\sqrt{2}}^{n+2}}{\sqrt{\pi n}}
209: on the number of generators needed for I_{w}, accompanying our
210: exponential upper bound of 2^{n}. Thus one would not be able to expect
211: short presentations for H^{*}(X_{w}) in general, at least in type A.

claims.text: The relevant two sets are those in Theorem 4.8, for \(v_{r,s,t,n}\), \(a=\min(n-r-i,r-j)\), \(b=\min(i,j)\), in the integral ring \(\Lambda/I_{r,n-r}\). [doi:10.1090/s0002-9947-2010-05163-3, lines 864-892]

groundings.excerpt:
864: Theorem 4.8 .
865: Given a bigrassmannian v=v_{r,s,t,n} in type A_{n-1} with \mathfrak{S}_{v}=s_{i^{j}}, let
866: \displaystyle a
867: \displaystyle:=\min(n-r-i,r-j)
868: \displaystyle b
869: \displaystyle:=\min(i,j).
870: Then J_{v} is generated as an ideal of
871: H^{\star}(G/P_{J},{\mathbb{Z}})\cong\Lambda/I_{r,n-r} by
872: (4.5)
873: \{s_{\mu}:i^{j}\subseteq\mu\subseteq((i+a)^{b},i^{j-b})\}.
874: Alternatively, J_{v} is generated by
875: (4.6)
876: \{s_{\mu}:i^{j}\subseteq\mu\subseteq(i^{j},b^{a})\}.
877: We delay our proof of Theorem 4.8 until Section 4.7 .
878: Note that in both of the asserted generating sets ( 4.5 ) and ( 4.6 ) for J_{v},
879: the shapes \mu indexing the generators s_{\mu} run through an interval between
880: the j\times i rectangular shape i^{j} and the disjoint union of i^{j} with a
881: smaller rectangle of shape a\times b or b\times a.
882: In ( 4.5 ) the smaller rectangle is to the right
883: of the rectangle i^{j}, with both top-justified, while in ( 4.6 ) the
884: smaller rectangle is below the rectangle i^{j}, with both left-justified.
885: Thus in both cases, the generating sets have size \binom{a+b}{a}
886: and consist of generators whose multiset of degrees
887: have generating function
888: \sum_{\mu}q^{|\mu|}=q^{ij}\left[\begin{matrix}a+b\\
889: a\end{matrix}\right]_{q},
890: where \left[\begin{matrix}a+b\\
891: a\end{matrix}\right]_{q} is a q- binomial coefficient or Gaussian polynomial
892: [ M91 , I.2 Exer. 3] .

claims.text: **Conjecture 4.10** states: “The two generating sets for the ideal \(J_{v_{r,s,t,n}}\) given in Theorem 4.8 are both minimal”; RWY reports verification for \(r\le4\) and \(n-r\le5\). [doi:10.1090/s0002-9947-2010-05163-3, lines 938-946]

groundings.excerpt:
938: 4.5. A minimality conjecture
939: As we shall see in a moment,
940: our generators for I_{w} are not minimal. However,
941: we believe the following holds:
942: Conjecture 4.10 .
943: The two generating sets for the ideal J_{v_{r,s,t,n}} given in Theorem 4.8

claims.text: RWY separately conjectures that \(M/\Lambda_+M\) requires \(\binom{a+b}{a}\) generators and suspects the stronger freeness statement \(M/\Lambda_+M\cong\mathbb Z^{\binom{a+b}{a}}\), adding that a proof had eluded them. [doi:10.1090/s0002-9947-2010-05163-3, lines 956-975]

groundings.excerpt:
956: The size of any minimal generating set of a homogeneous ideal is
957: well-defined. This is implied by the following well-known fact:
958: Proposition 4.11 .
959: Let R be a commutative ring, and \Lambda=\oplus_{n\geq 0}\Lambda_{n} a graded, connected R-algebra, meaning that \Lambda_{0}=R and \Lambda_{i}\Lambda_{j}\subset\Lambda_{i+j}. Let M be a
960: graded \Lambda-module, with degrees bounded below, meaning that
961: M=\oplus_{n\geq N}M_{n} for some N\in{\mathbb{Z}}, and \Lambda_{i}M_{j}\subset M_{i+j}.
962: Then a set of homogeneous elements \{m_{i}\}_{i=1}^{t} generate M as a \Lambda-module
963: if and only if their images \{\bar{m_{i}}\}_{i=1}^{t} span M/\Lambda_{+}M as a R-module.
964: In particular, \{m_{i}\}_{i=1}^{t} form a minimal \Lambda-generating set with respect to
965: inclusion for M if and only if \{\bar{m_{i}}\}_{i=1}^{t} form a minimal R-spanning
966: set for M/\Lambda_{+}M.
967: In our setting, the well-definedness follows by setting
968: \Lambda=\oplus_{n\geq 0}\Lambda_{n} to be the graded ring of
969: symmetric functions with {\mathbb{Z}} coefficients and setting
970: M=J_{v_{r,s,t,n}}, so that the {\mathbb{Z}}-module M/\Lambda_{+}M
971: is a finitely generated abelian group.
972: Thus we conjecture that this abelian group M/\Lambda_{+}M requires
973: \binom{a+b}{a} generators, and in fact, we suspect that
974: M/\Lambda_{+}M\cong{\mathbb{Z}}^{\binom{a+b}{a}}. So far a proof
975: has eluded us.

claims.text: The immediately posed concatenation question is answered negatively in RWY itself: minimal generating sets for the \(J_v\) need not concatenate to a minimal set for \(I_w\); \(w=1243\) is the displayed counterexample. [doi:10.1090/s0002-9947-2010-05163-3, lines 976-994]

groundings.excerpt:
976: Example 4.12 .
977: Since I_{w}=\sum_{v\in{\mathcal{E}}(w)}J_{v}, and since we have
978: conjectured that the generating sets provided by Theorem 4.8
979: for J_{v} are minimal, one might wonder whether their
980: concatentation gives a minimal generating set of I_{w}. As mentioned above, this turns
981: out to be false in general.
982: The smallest counterexample is given by w=1243, which has
983: {\mathcal{E}}(w)=\{v_{1}=2134,v_{2}=1324\}
984: The generating sets given in Theorem 4.8 for the ideals J_{v_{1}} and J_{v_{2}} are
985: \displaystyle J_{v_{1}}
986: \displaystyle=\langle s_{(1)}(x_{1})\rangle=\langle x_{1}\rangle
987: \displaystyle J_{v_{2}}
988: \displaystyle=\langle s_{(1)}(x_{1},x_{2}),\quad s_{(2)}(x_{1},x_{2})\rangle\quad\text{ or }\quad\langle s_{(1)}(x_{1},x_{2}),\quad s_{(1,1)}(x_{1},x_{2})\rangle
989: \displaystyle=\langle x_{1}+x_{2},\quad x_{1}^{2}+x_{1}x_{2}+x_{2}^{2}\rangle\text{ or }\langle x_{1}+x_{2},\quad x_{1}x_{2}\rangle,
990: and in each case they minimally generate their ideals J_{v_{i}}.
991: However, concatenating them gives non-minimal generating sets for I_{w}, namely
992: \displaystyle I_{w}=J_{v_{1}}+J_{v_{2}}
993: \displaystyle=\langle x_{1},\quad x_{1}+x_{2},\quad x_{1}^{2}+x_{1}x_{2}+x_{2}^{2}\rangle\quad\text{ or }\quad\langle x_{1},\quad x_{1}+x_{2},\quad x_{1}x_{2}\rangle
994: \displaystyle\left(=\langle x_{1},\quad x_{1}+x_{2}\rangle\right).
